name: NumberFormatter

examples.title: Currencies
examples.code:
<Paragraph>
  Order total:{' '}
  <NumberFormatter
    value={8456.4}
    locale="en-US"
    format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }}
  />
</Paragraph>

examples.title: Percentages, Units and Signs
examples.code:
<DescriptionList>
  <DescriptionList.Item
    label="Conversion rate"
    value={
      <NumberFormatter
        value={0.125}
        locale="en-US"
        format={{ style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
      />
    }
  />
  <DescriptionList.Item
    label="Average speed"
    value={
      <NumberFormatter
        value={12}
        locale="en-US"
        format={{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilometer-per-hour' }}
      />
    }
  />
  <DescriptionList.Item
    label="Change"
    value={
      <NumberFormatter
        value={0.034}
        locale="en-US"
        format={{
          style: 'percent',
          signDisplay: 'exceptZero',
          maximumFractionDigits: 1,
        }}
      />
    }
  />
</DescriptionList>

examples.title: Compact Notation
examples.code:
<DescriptionList>
  {['en-US', 'fr-FR', 'ja-JP', 'de-DE'].map(locale => (
    <DescriptionList.Item
      key={locale}
      label={locale}
      value={
        <NumberFormatter
          value={123456}
          locale={locale}
          format={{ notation: 'compact' }}
        />
      }
    />
  ))}
</DescriptionList>

examples.title: In a LocaleProvider
examples.code:
<LocaleProvider locale="fr-FR">
  <Paragraph>
    Vitesse moyenne :{' '}
    <NumberFormatter
      value={1234.5}
      format={{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilometer-per-hour' }}
    />
  </Paragraph>
</LocaleProvider>

accessibility:
- **No role:** `<data>` maps to no role, so a screen reader reads the formatted text, with the
  locale's currency symbol, percent sign, units and sign, as it would read the same text anywhere
  else.
- **Compact notation** is read as written ("123K"). Show the exact figure too where it matters.
- **Language:** a `locale` that differs from the page's language changes how the number is
  written, not the voice that reads it. A passage in another language still needs `lang` on its
  container, which `LocaleProvider` sets.
- **Not live:** a changing value isn't announced. Wrap the one figure that should be in a
  `role="status"` element, as in [A Number That Changes](https://bestax.io/docs/api/elements/numberformatter#a-number-that-changes).
- **Not color alone:** for a rise or a fall, write the sign with `signDisplay`, so the direction
  doesn't depend on a `textColor`.
summary: The `NumberFormatter` component writes a number the way a locale writes it, such as a price, a percentage or a count, in a `<data>` element that keeps the number itself in its `value`. It formats with `Intl.NumberFormat`, in its own `locale`, else the `LocaleProvider`'s around it, else the runtime's, with `format` as the options. The `<data>` has no role and no class of its own, so a screen reader reads the formatted text and it takes the look of the text around it. For text outside JSX, such as an `aria-label`, `useNumberFormat` gives the same formatting as a function.

parts.summary: The `NumberFormatter` component writes a number the way a locale writes it, such as a price, a percentage or a count, in a `<data>` element that keeps the number itself in its `value`. It formats with `Intl.NumberFormat`, in its own `locale`, else the `LocaleProvider`'s around it, else the runtime's, with `format` as the options. The `<data>` has no role and no class of its own, so a screen reader reads the formatted text and it takes the look of the text around it. For text outside JSX, such as an `aria-label`, `useNumberFormat` gives the same formatting as a function.

props.name: value
props.description: The number. The text is what `Intl.NumberFormat` writes for it, `NaN` and `Infinity` included. The `<data>` element's `value` attribute holds it as JavaScript writes a number with `String()`, which `Number()` reads back: `1234.5`, `1e+21` for a very large one and `1e-7` for a very small one, `NaN`, `Infinity`, and `-0` with its sign.

props.name: format
props.description: `Intl.NumberFormat` options: a currency, a percentage, a unit, compact notation, the fraction digits, the sign. Options `Intl` refuses, such as `style: 'currency'` with no `currency`, throw its error.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale tag. Unset, it's the `locale` of a `LocaleProvider` around it, and with neither, the runtime's own. On a server render that's the server's, so give it a locale, here or through a `LocaleProvider`, where the server's and the browser's can differ. A tag `Intl` refuses, such as `"en_US"`, is ignored, with a warning in development, as `LocaleProvider` ignores one.
